turns.en: Hello, my name's Siân, I'm one of the nurses looking after you today. What's your name, and what would you like me to call you?
turns.cy: Helô — Siân dw i, un o'r nyrsys sy'n edrych ar eich ôl chi heddiw. Be ydy'ch enw chi, a be liciech chi i mi'ch galw chi?
chunks: HG17 — Welsh identifies by fronted predicate, not by possessing a name
I'm one of the nurses looking after you today
un o'r nyrsys sy'n edrych ar eich ôl chi heddiw
the English participial relative becomes a sy'-relative; 'look after' is the conjugated ar eich ôl chi
what would you like me to call you?
be liciech chi i mi'ch galw chi?
HG17 verbatim; the i mi + verbal-noun clause carries English's ECM

turns.en: Margaret. But everyone calls me Peggy.
turns.cy: Margaret. Ond Peggy mae pawb yn fy ngalw i.
chunks: Ond Peggy mae pawb yn fy ngalw i
the name fronts for focus; the nasal mutation fy ngalw is absorbed inside the chunk

turns.en: Lovely to meet you, Peggy. I've got a few little jobs to do with you this morning, if that's alright.
turns.cy: Braf eich cyfarfod chi, Peggy. Mae gen i chydig o jobsys bach i'w gneud efo chi bore 'ma, os ydy hynny'n iawn.
chunks: HG18 — the object pre-poses as a possessive before the verbal noun
I've got a few little jobs to do with you this morning
Mae gen i chydig o jobsys bach i'w gneud efo chi bore 'ma
the mae gen i possessive; the i'w + verbal-noun purpose clause
south: mae … gyda fi — AND A REORDER
turns.southLine: Braf eich cwrdd chi, Peggy. Mae tipyn o jobsys bach gyda fi i'w gwneud gyda chi bore 'ma, os yw hynny'n iawn.

turns.en: Peggy's fine, everyone calls me Peggy. Right then, what's first?
turns.cy: Mae Peggy'n iawn — Peggy mae pawb yn fy ngalw i. Reit 'ta, be sy gynta?
chunks: Peggy mae pawb yn fy ngalw i
as F01-S02 — one form for one intention

turns.en: First I just need to check your details. Can you tell me your date of birth?
turns.cy: Gynta, dw i jyst angen tsiecio'ch manylion chi. Fedrwch chi ddeud eich dyddiad geni wrtha i?
chunks: First I just need to check your details
Gynta, dw i jyst angen tsiecio'ch manylion chi
HG19 verbatim; tsiec- is the one check-lexeme (R7)
Can you tell me your date of birth?
Fedrwch chi ddeud eich dyddiad geni wrtha i?
the conjugated wrtha i lands clause-finally, where English puts 'me' early

turns.en: Third of March, nineteen forty-one. I'm no spring chicken.
turns.cy: Y trydydd o Fawrth, mil naw pedwar deg un. Dw i ddim yn ifanc bellach.
chunks: the ordinal takes the article; Mawrth soft-mutates after o
Welsh reads the year as a whole number, not as two pairs (R5, modern decimal)
Dw i ddim yn ifanc bellach
English's poultry idiom has no Welsh reflex; bellach carries the 'any more'

turns.en: Hello, I'm Siân, one of the nurses on today. And you are?
turns.cy: Helô — Siân dw i, un o'r nyrsys sy 'mlaen heddiw. A chithau?
chunks: one of the nurses on today
'on' as on-shift takes the sy' relative with 'mlaen
English strands a copula; Welsh uses the conjunctive pronoun, which does exactly this inviting job

turns.en: Sorry, love, what was your name again? I'm terrible with names.
turns.cy: Sori, del — be oedd eich enw chi eto? Dw i'n ofnadwy efo enwau.
chunks: be oedd eich enw chi eto?

turns.en: Siân. It's on my badge, look. Don't worry - there's a lot of us to remember.
turns.cy: Siân. Mae o ar fy mathodyn i, ylwch. Peidiwch â phoeni — mae 'na lot ohonan ni i'w cofio.
chunks: Mae o ar fy mathodyn i, ylwch
HG21 verbatim; ylwch is the northern look-tag
there's a lot of us to remember
mae 'na lot ohonan ni i'w cofio
the mae 'na existential + conjugated ohonan ni; English's partitive 'of us' conjugates

turns.en: Siân. There, I've got it now. My granddaughter's a Siân, as it happens.
turns.cy: Siân. Dyna ni — mae o gen i rŵan. Mae fy wyres i'n Siân, fel mae'n digwydd.
chunks: English's have-got relocates to the gen i possessive
English's indefinite article on a name erases
turns.southLine: Siân. Dyna ni — mae e gyda fi nawr. Mae fy wyres i'n Siân, fel mae'n digwydd.

turns.en: A good name to remember, then. Before we start, is there anything you need - water, another pillow?
turns.cy: Enw da i'w gofio, 'ta. Cyn i ni ddechra — oes 'na rywbeth dach chi angen? Dŵr, clustog arall?
chunks: A good name to remember, then
the English indefinite article erases; 'ta is the in-that-case tag (S1)
'anything' → rhywbeth in the existential offer; the any/some distinction erases (S9)
south: mae angen arnoch chi / chi'n moyn

turns.en: I'm fine as I am, thank you. Go on then, do your worst.
turns.cy: Dw i'n iawn fel dw i, diolch. Ewch amdani 'ta — gnewch eich gwaetha.
chunks: Dw i'n iawn fel dw i
English gapping does not survive — Welsh repeats the verb

turns.en: Hello, my name's Siân, I'm looking after you today. What would you like me to call you?
turns.cy: Helô — Siân dw i, a fi sy'n edrych ar eich ôl chi heddiw. Be liciech chi i mi'ch galw chi?
chunks: a fi sy'n edrych ar eich ôl chi heddiw
sy'-focus: Welsh identifies who, where English merely states
What would you like me to call you?
Be liciech chi i mi'ch galw chi?

turns.en: Are you with me all day, then? It's nice to see a friendly face.
turns.cy: Dach chi efo fi drwy'r dydd, 'ta? Mae'n neis gweld wyneb clên.
chunks: Are you with me all day, then?
Dach chi efo fi drwy'r dydd, 'ta?
It's nice to see a friendly face

turns.en: I'm here till eight tonight, so you're stuck with me. And if I'm not about, any of the team can help you.
turns.cy: Dw i yma tan wyth heno, felly dach chi'n sownd efo fi. Ac os dydw i ddim o gwmpas, mi fedar unrhyw un o'r tîm eich helpu chi.
chunks: Dw i yma tan wyth heno
felly dach chi'n sownd efo fi
the same sownd stuck-lexeme as the opener's 'if we get stuck'
Ac os dydw i ddim o gwmpas
any of the team can help you
mi fedar unrhyw un o'r tîm eich helpu chi
3sg mi fedar; the eich…chi echo object

turns.en: Till eight! That's a long old day. I don't know how you do it.
turns.cy: Tan wyth! Mae hynna'n ddiwrnod hir. Wn i ddim sut dach chi'n ei gneud hi.
chunks: English's affectionate 'old' has no Welsh reflex here — erased
I don't know how you do it
Wn i ddim sut dach chi'n ei gneud hi
the irregular short gwybod negative; the feminine dummy object hi

turns.en: Ah, it flies by. Right - can you tell me your date of birth, so I know I've got the right person?
turns.cy: A, mae o'n hedfan. Reit — fedrwch chi ddeud eich dyddiad geni wrtha i, i mi fod yn siŵr mai chi ydy'r person iawn?
chunks: English's particle 'by' has no Welsh reflex
can you tell me your date of birth
fedrwch chi ddeud eich dyddiad geni wrtha i
so I know I've got the right person?
i mi fod yn siŵr mai chi ydy'r person iawn?
HG20 verbatim — the mai-cleft, and 'know' becomes 'be sure', dodging the gwybod/nabod fork (S5)

turns.en: Course. Twelfth of June, nineteen thirty-eight.
turns.cy: Siŵr iawn. Y deuddegfed o Fehefin, mil naw tri deg wyth.
chunks: the clipped form is its own known, kept distinct from 'Of course' → Wrth gwrs
the year as a whole number (R5)
